This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 07.08.2014, passed in M.V.C.No.1236/2013, on the file of the Senior Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Maddur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Senior Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Maddur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts:
2. On 23.06.2013 at about 3.30 p.m., the injured / minor claimant was playing on the ground in front of the house of one Jayaramu at K.Bellur Village, Maddur Taluk.
At that time, one TATA ACE Goods Vehicle bearing MFA No. 7600 OF 2015 registration No.KA-11-A-0363 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed came from Thorechakanahalli road and dashed against the minor claimant and caused the accident.
Due to the impact the claimant sustained grievous and multiple injuries.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant-claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act,
claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.5,85,600/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 - being owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle jointly and severally, liable to pay the compensation.
Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondents and perused the materials on record.

sentences.text:
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
Pain and Suffering & : Rs. 3,00,000/-
 Loss of Amenities  Medical Expenses : Rs. 2,85,600/-
 TOTAL : Rs. 5,85,600/-
6.
In the present case, the appellant-claimant is a minor boy aged four years old had sustained injuries.
The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.5,85,600/- in total along with interest.
The Tribunal has followed the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun v/s.
Div Manager
National Ins Co Ltd1 (hereinafter referred to as 'Master Mallikarjun' case for brevity),

and considering the evidence that the claimant (2014) 14 SCC 396 MFA No. 7600 OF 2015 had sustained disability at 23% towards whole-body and accordingly granted a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head 'Pain And Sufferings' And 'Loss Of Amenities'.
As per Master Mallikarjun case stated supra it is found to be correct and appropriately awarded compensation.

Further, the Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.2,85,600/-
towards 'Medical Expenses and Hospital Charges' which are as per actual bills produced.
Therefore, the same is kept in-tact.

7. But the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head 'Discomfort,
Inconvenience and Loss of earning to the parents during the period of Hospitalization' and towards 'Future Medical Expenses' for correcting the mal-union if any and other incidental expenses.

Therefore, under these heads towards 'Discomfort, Inconvenience and Loss of earning to the parents during the period of Hospitalization' and also for Future Medical Expenses and Other Incidental Expense a additional sum of Rs.50,000/-
MFA No. 7600 OF 2015 is awarded by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun case stated supra.
8.
Accordingly, the appellant-claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,35,600/- as against Rs.5,85,600/-.

The appellant-claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.50,000/-
(Rs. 6,35,600 - 5,85,600) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
However, the appellant-claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 293 days, in filing the appeal.

9. Accordingly, I pass the following:
